correctness.rationale: Proposition 5.2 source vertex strings give exactly 9 branches at block 0 (five same, four up), and 6k+13 branches at block k>=1 (2(k+2) down/up and 2k+5 same), each affine onto a full unit block, so every block itinerary under uniform initial density has the displayed Markov transition law. Direct balance pi_k P_(k,k+1)=4/9 determines pi0=1 and pi_k=2(6k+13)/(9(k+2)). Symmetric birth/death probabilities imply P_k(T_L<T_0)=k/L; recurrent but no summable invariant measure, hence null recurrent. Renewal with infinite mean yields zero occupation frequency of every finite block. Under psi, this proves weak empirical delta_1; recurrence plus positive full-branch cylinders ensures infinitely many visits to each rational interval, hence dense orbit. A probability absolutely continuous invariant law would contradict this full Lebesgue delta_1 empirical limit. Independently checked exact branch counts, detailed balance and harmonic identities for finite k,L; these cannot replace the recurrence/ergodic proofs.

value.rationale: A natural explicit counterpoint to topological mixing: typical orbit is dense and recurrent in every interval but spends zero asymptotic fraction in every finite core, producing a unique endpoint physical probability without pointwise attraction. The exact reversible density and null recurrence provide reusable quantitative invariant and a transparent infinite-ergodic example.

limitations: Almost-everywhere rather than all initial orbits; convergence of empirical probabilities is weak, not pointwise convergence to the endpoint.
No return-time distributional limit or rate, and no assertion about all mixing infinite-entropy interval maps.
